newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries end up after solid 5-yr note sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries end up after solid 5-yr note sale.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries closed higher Wednesday as solid, broad-based demand for a Treasury auction of five-year notes lured domestic and foreign investors back into the market after a morning selloff, analysts said.
The 30-year benchmark T-bond ended up 11/32 at 101-6/32. Its yield fell to 6.41 percent against 6.44 percent Tuesday.

The market was also bolstered by strong activity from Asian accounts seeking a safe-haven in U.S. Treasuries after news that Japan's Ministry of Finance said it would order Hanwa Bank to suspend most of its business.

An official at Japan's MOF said Hanwa's suspension was due to the bank's failure to recover bad loans. Separately, Japanese sources said the Bank of Japan will set up an emergency fund to prevent a crisis at Hanwa Bank.
"The story on the Japanese bank helped the dollar against the yen and prompted some Asian accounts to buy Treasuries," said an analyst at a major investment bank here.
Also, pundits said concerns sorrounding the Japanese banking system are likely to prevent the Bank of Japan from raising interest rates in the very short-term.
That sentiment bolstered the notion the U.S. dollar may remain firm against the yen and that dollar-denominated assets might still be a good investment option.

"To the extent that the dollar has been under some pressure lately, it will take some of that pressure off. It'll ease fears of lessened foreign demand for Treasuries," said Lee Youngdahl, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston Co. Inc.

Analysts were also optimistic after the Treasury auction of $12.5 billion of five-year notes met solid demand and was placed at a lower-than-expected yield of 5.950 percent. Non-competitive bids totalled $310 million.

"We had very good buying of this issue all day long ... the bid-to-cover ratio was much better than usual at 2.86 versus an average of 2.3," said Patrick Dimick, Treasury market strategist at UBS Securities.
Analysts said they noticed very broad-based buying of U.S. Treasuries after the five-year note auction results were released in early afternoon trade.

Hedge funds, foreign central banks and some retailers were seen as very active players. Thus, analysts noted some players unwinding steepening trades with two- and five-year notes by buying the new five-year securities in the auction.

A bullish technical environment also provided underpinning. Experts said charts have shown the formation of a small bullish triangle pattern over the last few days, which could indicate the market is ripe for a fresh rally.
The consensus among chart bulls hints the yield on the benchmark bond may slide to 6.30 percent over the next seven days or so.

In the morning, the market opened lower following some selling overnight on a weaker dollar and on jitters over news reports that an unidentified Federal Reserve official was worried about inflation and a drop in long-term rates.
Total volume as measured by GovPX was $88.638 billion.
GovPX publishes real-time Treasury prices and volume from five of the six intra-dealer brokers, representing 65 percent of the intra-dealers trades.
The three-month bill rate closed down one basis point at 5.02 percent. The six-month bill rate fell one point to 5.05 percent. The year bill rate rose one point to 5.12 percent.

The 2-year note closed flat at 99-30/32, yielding 5.66 percent. The 5-year note was up 4/32 at 101-13/32 to yield 5.92 percent. The 10-year note was up 7/32 at 102-22/32, yielding 6.13 percent. -- 212-859-1676
